requirements.title: A pointer component contributes its association rather than a copied target value
requirements.source: 7.5.8, p1.pointer-component, p1.pointer-association-value; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: For a pointer component, its component value is its pointer association. A data target's contents are not a replacement for that association, and a procedure pointer denotes its procedure association rather than an evaluated function result. Disassociated and associated states must be distinguished without querying an undefined association. The operation used to observe or transfer this value retains its own pointer-assignment and interface conditions.
requirements.oracle: Four declared runtime-effect connections each reuse the single complete S10_2_1_3_024_valid program. ASSOCIATED compares the copied scalar/strided-array pointers with live named targets and the procedure pointer with double_value under its explicit interface; mutation checks scalar=41 and values(4)=43. Explicit NULLIFY precedes the second copy and all three disassociation guards. The program retains S10.2.1.3-024 ownership and runs once per configuration, not once per link. Declared connections are not reviewed links or passing effects: source, case/oracle, connection and complete per-configuration execution gates remain separate.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Read only defined values and independently established allocation/association states. Keep pointer targets alive, use exact eligible procedure interfaces, guard allocation before dependent inquiries, and do not dereference null or undefined pointers. A component value is not an ABI layout or a byte encoding. This paragraph does not independently prescribe how every operation copies a pointer; the canonical assignment rules supply that operation. No allocation-address, target-value equality or opaque C descriptor oracle is authorized.

requirements.title: An allocatable component's value includes conditional allocation characteristics and data
requirements.source: 7.5.8, p1.allocatable-status, p1.allocated-condition, p1.allocated-dynamic-type, p1.allocated-type-parameters, p1.allocated-bounds, p1.allocated-value; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: An allocatable component contributes its allocation status. When it is allocated, its component value additionally includes dynamic type, type parameter values, bounds and data value. The allocated-only qualification does not authorize reading absent data or inferring an allocation's physical address. Allocation, assignment, inquiry and defined-assignment operations retain their separately specified semantics.
requirements.oracle: Each of six declared runtime-effect connections has exactly one complete canonical member. Plain S10_2_1_3_029_valid supplies allocated-to-unallocated and both-unallocated status guards, not its finalization variant. S10_2_1_3_030_valid supplies allocation-first guards, exact child and REAL(kind=dp) guards with dp=KIND(0.0d0), length 3, and nonempty bounds -2:0; its empty controls observe allocated status, size zero and length zero, not hidden empty bounds. S10_2_1_3_032_valid alone supplies allocated data values, including extension and nested array literals, with the dynamic-only assignment binding excluded and a source-preserving mutation. No connection combines partial facts from several programs. Existing S10 owners, complete-case execution, independent source/case/connection review and per-configuration qualification remain required.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Read only defined values and independently established allocation/association states. Keep pointer targets alive, use exact eligible procedure interfaces, guard allocation before dependent inquiries, and do not dereference null or undefined pointers. A component value is not an ABI layout or a byte encoding. This definition is not an independent deep-copy or deallocation requirement, and it does not promise an allocation can never fail. Unallocated components do not acquire observable payloads by this paragraph.

requirements.title: An ordinary component contributes its data value
requirements.source: 7.5.8, p1.nonpointer-nonallocatable, p1.ordinary-component-value; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF106, printed92.
requirements.definition: For a component with neither POINTER nor ALLOCATABLE, the component value is its data value. This includes intrinsic data, a nested derived value and array-valued data under their own type, parameter, shape and definedness rules. It does not make general derived-type equality intrinsic or override a separately applicable defined assignment.
requirements.oracle: Three declared runtime-effect connections each reuse complete S10_2_1_3_026_valid without a new program or owner. Its named initializations and independent guards check tag=17, text='abc', true flag, nested scalar (23,1.5), and array elements (31,2.5)/(43,-3.5); changing the copied first array integer to -1 leaves the source at 31. Neither local derived type supplies defined assignment. The source/fixture/connection gates and complete single-configuration run remain prerequisites; three member occurrences do not mean three executions or three currently qualified effects.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Read only defined values and independently established allocation/association states. Keep pointer targets alive, use exact eligible procedure interfaces, guard allocation before dependent inquiries, and do not dereference null or undefined pointers. A component value is not an ABI layout or a byte encoding. Defined assignment can legitimately change the destination value; S10.2.1.3-025 is not interchangeable with the no-matching-binding case. The p2 value-set definition remains fully accounted without a no-op execution.

accounting.rationale: PDF106 lines2-6 divide the semantic component-value definition into pointer, allocatable and ordinary branches, retaining the allocated-only condition.

PDF106 lines7-8 define the value set by possible sequences of the type's component values. This is a normative semantic model, not permission to enumerate arbitrary bit patterns or a new requirement for intrinsic derived-type equality, storage layout or an empty executable. The p1 branches and canonical operations provide the finite observable witnesses; 7.2 and7.5.4.7 retain parameter dependence and component ordering.

review_rationale: Retain the original complete2base/14fine-unit value decomposition and normative p2definition from batch052. Independently reviewed proposal2d6cd9c and receiptfd016ab69d3a92486163c7154c95c9ffeda72e57ea2f72c0f62dca7d69f4d38d in doc/source_audits/batch_057.json justify thirteen finite singleton runtime-effect connections over five unchanged S10canonical programs. No p2classifier, ABI/representation proof, partial-program combination or new program is created. Each connection has a separate content-bound review.
